summary:
**AstraVitals – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring System**

AstraVitals is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring and early-warning system designed to address the challenges of monitoring astronaut health during space missions. It combines a web-based health intelligence platform with a wearable health-monitoring watch to track vital signs and identify potential health risks before they become critical.

The wearable watch is designed around an optical PPG sensor for heart rate and SpO₂ monitoring, a skin-temperature sensor, and an accelerometer for activity tracking. It also incorporates a microcontroller, wireless Bluetooth connectivity, a rechargeable battery, and a sensor-contact quality mechanism to ensure reliable readings.

The AstraVitals software provides real-time-style health dashboards, health trends, alerts, an interactive body map, radiation monitoring, sleep and wellbeing tracking, medical check-ins, mission reports, and offline data support. It uses health indicators and intelligent risk-assessment logic to help identify abnormalities and recommend further health checks.

Our goal is to improve astronaut safety, enable early health-risk detection, and support informed medical decisions during long-duration space missions, where immediate access to healthcare professionals is limited.
details:
AstraVitals – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

AstraVitals is a smart astronaut health-monitoring system designed to support astronaut safety during space missions, particularly long-duration missions where immediate medical assistance may not be available.

The project combines a wearable health-monitoring watch with a web-based health management platform. The wearable watch is designed to collect important physiological data, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), skin temperature, and physical activity. The collected information can be transmitted wirelessly to the software dashboard, where it can be monitored, analyzed, and presented through visual charts and health indicators.

The platform includes a health dashboard, vital-sign monitoring, investigation records, health alerts, radiation monitoring, sleep and wellbeing tracking, medical check-ins, mission reports, and offline support. Its risk-assessment system helps identify unusual health readings and highlights potential health concerns that may require attention.

2. What are the benefits?

  • Enables continuous monitoring of important health indicators.
  • Supports early identification of abnormal vital signs.
  • Helps astronauts and medical teams make informed health-related decisions.
  • Provides organized health records and historical trends.
  • Reduces dependence on immediate access to medical professionals.
  • Supports astronaut wellbeing through activity, sleep, and health monitoring.
  • Provides an integrated platform for health information and mission-related monitoring.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our intended impact is to improve astronaut health, safety, and wellbeing during space exploration. By combining wearable technology with intelligent health-monitoring software, AstraVitals aims to make health monitoring more accessible, organized, and proactive.

In the future, the system could support space agencies in monitoring astronauts during extended missions, identifying potential medical risks earlier, and improving emergency preparedness. The technology could also be adapted for remote healthcare and patient monitoring on Earth.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, and software were used?

Software and development tools:

  • React.js – Developing the interactive user interface.
  • JavaScript – Implementing application functionality and monitoring logic.
  • HTML5 and CSS3 – Structuring and styling the platform.
  • Vite – Development environment and build tool.
  • Lucide React – Interface icons and visual elements.
  • Git and GitHub – Version control and project collaboration.
  • VS Code – Code development and debugging.

Proposed wearable hardware:

  • ESP32 microcontroller – Processing sensor data and enabling wireless communication.
  • MAX30102 PPG sensor – Measuring heart rate and estimating blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂).
  • Temperature sensor – Monitoring skin temperature.
  • MPU6050 accelerometer and gyroscope – Tracking movement and physical activity.
  • Bluetooth/Wi-Fi connectivity – Transmitting collected data.
  • Rechargeable lithium battery – Powering the wearable device.
  • OLED display – Displaying essential health information directly on the watch.

The physical hardware integration and live sensor-data connection are intended development components; the current software prototype demonstrates the monitoring interface and functionality.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

AstraVitals is creative because it brings together wearable technology, health analytics, astronaut wellbeing, and mission monitoring in one integrated concept. Instead of focusing only on displaying vital signs, it aims to provide a broader picture of astronaut health through health trends, risk indicators, alerts, radiation monitoring, and medical records.

The combination of a wearable watch and an interactive health dashboard creates a practical approach to remote health supervision. The system is also designed with future expansion in mind, including real-time sensor integration, more advanced health-risk prediction, and intelligent medical assistance.

6. What factors did our team consider?

During development, our team considered:

  • Accuracy: The importance of collecting reliable physiological measurements.
  • Safety: Identifying abnormal readings and potential health risks.
  • Usability: Creating a simple, understandable interface for astronauts and medical teams.
  • Real-time monitoring: Supporting timely access to health information.
  • Connectivity: Considering wireless communication and offline functionality.
  • Power efficiency: Designing a wearable device suitable for extended use.
  • Comfort and portability: Ensuring that the watch is lightweight and practical for everyday use.
  • Scalability: Making the system adaptable to future hardware and software improvements.
  • Space environment: Considering radiation exposure, limited medical resources, and the challenges of long-duration space missions.

Overall, AstraVitals aims to bridge the gap between wearable health technology and intelligent astronaut healthcare, contributing to safer and more sustainable human space exploration.

Current Functional Status of AstraVitals

AstraVitals currently has a functional web-based software prototype developed using React.js, JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3. The platform is designed to support astronaut health monitoring through an interactive dashboard and multiple health-management modules.

Currently Functional Features:

  • Health Dashboard: Displays astronaut health information, vital-sign indicators, and monitoring summaries.
  • Vital Signs Monitoring: Displays heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, and other health parameters using prototype data.
  • Health Risk Assessment: Uses programmed assessment logic to identify potential health concerns based on available readings.
  • Health Alerts: Displays warnings for abnormal readings and potential health risks.
  • Investigation Module: Provides an interface for viewing and managing medical investigation information.
  • Radiation Monitoring: Includes a dedicated interface for radiation-related monitoring.
  • Sleep and Wellbeing: Provides sections for tracking sleep and general astronaut wellbeing.
  • Medical Records: Organizes health information and medical check-in records.
  • Mission Reports: Provides reporting functionality for reviewing health-monitoring information.
  • Offline Support: Includes offline-oriented functionality to improve accessibility when internet connectivity is limited.
  • Navigation and Settings: Provides interactive navigation between the platform's different modules.

Wearable Watch – Hardware Component:

AstraVitals also incorporates a proposed wearable health-monitoring watch designed around an ESP32 microcontroller. Its planned hardware components include a MAX30102 sensor for heart rate and SpO₂ measurement, a temperature sensor for skin-temperature monitoring, an MPU6050 accelerometer and gyroscope for movement tracking, an OLED display for presenting health readings, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi connectivity for data transmission, and a rechargeable lithium battery for portable operation.

Current Hardware Status:

The wearable watch hardware architecture has been identified, but physical sensor integration and live data transmission to the software dashboard are not yet confirmed as functional. The current software prototype demonstrates the intended monitoring interface using prototype data.

Overall Project Status:

AstraVitals is currently a functional software prototype with a proposed wearable hardware component. Its objective is to combine wearable health monitoring, health-risk assessment, medical records, and mission-related health information into one integrated platform. Future development will focus on physical watch integration, real-time sensor data collection, wireless communication, and more advanced health-risk prediction to improve astronaut safety during long-duration space missions.
